# M3.9 -- prove a bot can kill something AND LOOT THE CORPSE.
#
# COPY of m39_hunt_armed.txt (do not edit that file) with a looting attempt
# appended after the kill. Everything through "say the fight is over" is
# unchanged from m39_hunt_armed.txt; see that file's comments for why an
# armed fresh fighter, why real wilderness and not a farm, and why the wolf
# body ids below are read from the CHARDEF headers rather than generic UO
# documentation.
#
# RUN AS AN ARMED FIGHTER SESSION (53+ / RevolutionFighter03+).
#
# THE LOOT STEP IS WHERE THIS SCENARIO EARNS ITS NAME, AND IT IS WHERE IT
# STOPS SHORT. Read src/bot/Scenario.cpp's `remember` handling (the
# pack_graphic / carried_graphic / world_graphic / mobile_* branches,
# Scenario.cpp:1055-1130) and Client::FindItem's SearchZone enum
# (Client.h:1154, Client.cpp:3773-3818) end to end before assuming the
# scenario DSL can do this:
#
#   kZoneBackpack -- ALWAYS PlayerEquipSerialAt(kLayerBackpack), i.e. the
#                    bot's OWN worn backpack. Never an arbitrary container.
#   kZoneEquip    -- the bot's own worn gear.
#   kZoneWorld    -- top-level dynamic items_ (things lying directly on the
#                    ground), which is how `world_graphic` finds the corpse
#                    ITSELF below -- but a corpse's CONTENTS are not in
#                    items_, they are in a second map keyed by container
#                    serial (containerItems_[corpse_serial], populated by the
#                    0x3C handler, Client.cpp:1398-1435) that nothing in the
#                    scenario Op set can search.
#
# `pack_graphic`/`carried_graphic` are hard-wired to the PLAYER's backpack
# serial specifically (Client::FindBackpackItemByGraphic,
# Client::FindItemByGraphic, both call PlayerEquipSerialAt(kLayerBackpack)
# directly) -- there is no "pack_graphic, but for THIS container" variant,
# and Scenario::Resolve()'s token grammar (Scenario.cpp:147-195: @name,
# self, backpack, bank, vendor*, vendor_sell_graphic:<hex>,
# vendor_graphic:<hex>, a bare hex/decimal literal) has nothing that reads
# containerItems_ for a bound-but-not-the-backpack serial either. A corpse's
# item serials are assigned by the server at spawn time, so they cannot be
# hardcoded as a literal the way a vendor's stock can be named by graphic --
# vendor_graphic: works only because VendorOffer() is a SEPARATE list the
# client already special-cases, exactly the kind of special-casing a corpse
# does not get.
#
# The underlying engine capability to do this EXISTS and is proven working:
# Client::SendTakeToBackpack(serial, qty) (Client.h:684) explicitly "lift
# item from ANY open container -> backpack", and it is exposed to this
# codebase's JS scripting layer as Player.take(serial, qty) plus
# Player.containerItems(serial) (src/js/ClientBindings.cpp:486-556, the
# latter literally commented "items array from any open container (e.g. the
# bank box...)"). So Sphere-side and Client-engine-side, looting a corpse is
# just "open it, list containerItems_[corpse], take the one you want" -- the
# gap is entirely that the PLAIN-TEXT .txt Scenario interpreter this
# milestone's runner drives (run_m25.ps1 only ever passes `--scenario
# X.txt`, there is no JS-script launch path wired to it) never got a
# `remember <name> container_graphic <container-bind> <graphic-list>` op (or
# equivalent) added to expose that JS capability to .txt scenarios.
#
# Per the M3.9 brief: that is a real C++ gap (in Scenario.cpp, not in
# Sphere), not a scenario-authoring puzzle to solve by cleverness, and this
# file does not invent a workaround. Everything below this point that CAN be
# proven with the existing Op set IS proven: the corpse is found by its
# universal graphic, walked to if needed, opened, and the 0x3C reply is
# waited for and will show up in the log as
# "[0x3C] container contents: N item(s)" -- real evidence that the corpse
# has loot sitting in it, one packet away from a pack that this interpreter
# cannot yet reach into.
#
# EXPECTED CONTENTS, READ FROM THE SHARD'S OWN DATA, NOT GENERIC UO DOCS:
# c_wolf_grey [CHARDEF 019] (c_monster_classic.scp:1197) carries
#     RESOURCES=1 i_ribs_raw,6 i_hide
# i_ribs_raw is ITEMDEF 009f1 (i_profession_cook_barkeep_baker.scp:991) --
# NOT one of the generic "raw meat" ids UO documentation usually gives.
# i_hide is ITEMDEF 01078 (i_profession_tailor_tanner.scp:349), DUPELIST
# 01079 for the piled graphic once more than one accumulates -- the same
# stacking trap M3.7's ore run hit, so a real container_graphic op would
# need to accept a comma list here exactly like pack_graphic does.

wait_world
sleep 2500
ensure_peace
gait run

request_skills
sleep 1500
skill_report

remember pack backpack
open @pack
wait_action
sleep 1500

# ------------------------------------------------------------- 1. arm ourself
remember blade pack_graphic 0x13FE,0x13FF
require blade
equip @blade 1
wait_action
sleep 2000
say armed

# --------------------------------------------------- 2. out to REAL wilderness
use_moongates on
travel_point 1265 1612
wait_travel
expect_travel ok
sleep 2000

say hunting wolves

# --------------------------------------------------------------- 3. find prey
# 0x0019 grey wolf  0x00E1 timber wolf  0x0017 dire wolf  0x0025 white wolf
# 0x003F cougar     0x00D6 panther -- read off the CHARDEF headers, see
# m39_hunt_armed.txt for the full history of why.
#
# THIS PATROL CHASES AS IT GOES, and m39_hunt_armed.txt's does not -- a real
# difference from the copied original, made for a reason found live and
# worth recording rather than silently fixing.
#
# loot3.console.txt (this file, this run) proves the miss: the scan at
# (1229,1655) [22:35:12.466] read "Timber Wolf 0x00015311" in the nearby
# list. m39_hunt_armed.txt's structure (which this scenario started as an
# exact copy of) does `remember prey`/`require prey` exactly ONCE, after the
# LAST waypoint of the sweep -- so that sighting was simply discarded, and by
# the next scan at (1210,1680) [22:35:24.297], ~31 tiles and ~13s later, the
# wolf had dropped out of the 18-tile view radius (viewRange_,
# Client.h:1119) and `remember prey` bound 0x00000000 [22:35:32.732]. The
# wolf did not vanish; the patrol out-ran it by walking two more waypoints
# further AWAY from where it was seen instead of turning toward it -- loot1
# and loot2 never even got a sighting, so this is the one run with hard
# evidence of the mechanism, not a guess.
#
# So here: after EVERY scan, try to bind prey and immediately try
# goto_mobile toward it. goto_mobile on an unbound (0x00000000) serial is a
# documented no-op -- Client::ActionGotoMobile logs "not in the mobile
# cache" and returns false without starting an action, so wait_action
# returns immediately (client.ActionBusy() was never set) -- so this costs
# nothing on the legs where nothing is sighted, and on the leg where
# something IS sighted it turns the bot toward it instead of away, the same
# way a real hunter reacts to spotting tracks instead of finishing a
# pre-planned loop first.
scan_mobiles
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1265 1612
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1272 1607
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1229 1655
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1210 1680
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1185 1698
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action

# The sweep is done. If something was ever sighted, the chases above have
# been closing on it the whole time, so give it a few more scan/chase
# cycles to close the last distance and settle in the mobile cache before
# the hard `require`.
loop 4
  scan_mobiles
  sleep 1200
  remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
  goto_mobile @prey
  wait_action
endloop

require prey

goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
sleep 1500

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ 4. kill it
mark_hp

war on
sleep 800
attack @prey
wait_action

loop 20
  goto_mobile @prey
  wait_action
  sleep 2500
endloop

scan_mobiles
sleep 2500

war off
sleep 1200
say the fight is over

# --------------------------------------------------------- 5. find the corpse
# i_corpse is ITEMDEF 02006 (runtime/scripts/items/i_char_icons.scp:20-27),
# and the comment on that itemdef says outright every corpse in the shard is
# created from this ONE item: "you only need to alter ITEMDEF 02006 since
# all corpses are created by that one item." So 0x2006 is not a guess and
# not per-creature the way the wolf body ids above are.
open @pack
wait_action
sleep 1000

remember corpse world_graphic 0x2006
require corpse

# No travel step here on purpose. The attack loop above re-issued
# goto_mobile every 2.5s to stay in melee range for the whole fight, so the
# corpse should spawn within container-open range of wherever the bot is
# standing when the loop ends. There is also no op that WOULD get us there
# if it did not: goto takes a literal x/y (the corpse's position is not
# known ahead of time), and travel_entity resolves only MOBILE serials via
# Client::MobilePosition (ClientTravel.cpp:254-265) -- a corpse is a world
# item, not in mobileCache_, so travel_entity @corpse would fail with "that
# mobile is not in view" even though the corpse is right there. If this
# `open` fails on range, that is real evidence of a second gap (no
# item-position travel primitive), not something to paper over with an
# invented workaround.
open @corpse
wait_action

# Give the 0x3C container-contents packet time to arrive. Client.cpp:1398's
# OnContainerContents handler logs "[0x3C] container contents: N item(s)"
# unconditionally, whatever N is -- that line in <tag>.log is the real
# evidence the corpse has loot sitting in it, one packet the interpreter
# received and stored (containerItems_[corpse]) but has no scenario Op to
# read back out.
sleep 3000

say corpse opened, contents on the wire, no scenario op can reach them yet

# --------------------------------------------------- 6. THE STEP THAT DOES NOT EXIST
#
# The brief's own instruction: prove the transfer with mark_item before and
# expect_item_gain after, the way m37_slice_b_minoc.txt does for smelted
# ingots. That pattern needs a `move <item-in-corpse> <amount> @pack` line,
# and <item-in-corpse> needs a `remember` mode that searches
# containerItems_[@corpse] by graphic (0x09F1 ribs, 0x1078/0x1079 hide) the
# same way `pack_graphic` searches containerItems_[player's own backpack].
# That remember mode does not exist -- see the file header. Writing
#     remember loot pack_graphic 0x09F1,0x1078,0x1079
# here would not be that mode; pack_graphic ignores @corpse entirely and
# would search the PLAYER'S backpack, silently binding whatever ribs/hide
# the bot happens to already be carrying (nothing, for a fresh fighter) --
# which is exactly the kind of invented, misleading workaround the brief
# said not to build. So this scenario stops here, deliberately, with the
# fight and the corpse both proven and the extraction left undone.

request_skills
sleep 1500
skill_report
sleep 1500
logout
